messages.content: There's a bird building a nest on our window ledge.
How lovely. Do you know what kind of bird it is?
I think it's a pigeon. My dad wants to remove it.
Pigeons often nest on ledges because they feel safe there. If the nest has no eggs yet, now is the easiest time to decide. Once there are eggs or chicks, moving the nest can harm them.
Can we keep it until the babies leave?
You could ask your dad about that. Pigeon chicks usually leave the nest about a month after hatching. Keeping that window shut and not touching the nest will help both your family and the birds.
I'm buying my first winter jacket on my own this weekend.
That's a nice step. Do you know how cold it gets where you live?
Not very cold, maybe ten degrees at night.
Then you don't need a heavy jacket. A light padded one or a fleece would be enough. Check that you can move your arms easily and that the zip runs smoothly.
Should I buy one size bigger?
A little room is good, so you can wear a sweater underneath. Try it on over a thick top in the shop. If the sleeves cover your hands, it is too big.
The old library in our area might close because hardly anyone visits.
That would be a loss for the neighbourhood. Do you use it yourself?
I used to, as a kid. I'd like to help keep it open.
You could start by asking the librarian what would help most. Some libraries run reading clubs, homework hours or story time for children, which bring people in.
I could run a story hour for little kids on Saturdays.
That is a lovely idea. Pick short picture books, keep each session to about forty-five minutes, and put up notices in the building and nearby shops. Even a few regular families can make a difference.
I'm flying alone for the first time to visit my aunt in Pune.
That is a big step. Do you know your flight time?
Yes, it's at six in the morning. I'm seventeen, by the way.
Then plan to reach the airport about two hours early, so around four. Keep your ID and ticket in one easy pocket. Pack your bag the night before, and check the rules for liquids in hand luggage.
What if I get lost inside the airport?

Airports have lots of signs and staff. Look for the screens showing your flight number and gate. If you are unsure, ask at the airline counter or any staff member. Text your aunt once you board and again when you land.
I have my first performance review next week and I don't know what to expect.
It's normal to feel unsure the first time. A review is usually a talk about what went well, what can improve and your goals. Have you been given a form to fill in?
Yes, they asked me to list my achievements.
Then think back over the year and write down specific things you did, with results if possible. For example, "Finished the report two days early" is better than "Worked hard."
What if they criticise me?
Listen calmly and take notes. Ask for an example if a point is unclear, and ask how you can improve. Treating feedback as information, not as an attack, usually makes the meeting go better.
I made a mistake in a report that went to a client. My stomach is in knots.

That feeling is awful, but mistakes like this happen to almost everyone at work. The best thing is to tell your manager quickly, explain what went wrong and suggest a fix. Owning it early usually counts for more than the mistake itself.
Should I contact the client myself?
Check with your manager first. Some companies want one person to talk to the client, and your manager may want to send the correction. Have a corrected version ready so the fix can go out fast.
What's the easiest way to keep my room tidy? It's always a mess by Friday.
Try a ten-minute tidy every evening instead of one big clean-up. Put clothes away, clear your desk and throw out rubbish. Small daily resets stop the mess from piling up.
My problem is clothes. They end up on my chair.

Many people have a "chair pile." Give yourself one hook or basket for clothes you will wear again, and put everything else in the wash or the cupboard straight away. A clear place for each thing makes tidying faster.
My dad wants me to teach him how to make a spreadsheet for the house budget.
That sounds like a useful project to do together. Has he used a computer much before?
A little. He can type and send emails.
That's a good start. Begin with the basics: rows go across, columns go down, and each box is a cell. Make a simple table with three columns: the item, the amount and the month.
How do we add up the totals?
Most spreadsheet programs have a sum formula. Select the cell below the amounts and type something like =SUM(B2:B10), which adds everything from B2 to B10. Show him once, then let him try it himself.
He keeps typing over the formulas by mistake.
That happens a lot. You could colour the formula cells light yellow, so he knows not to type there. Some programs also let you lock certain cells.
Thanks, he's actually enjoying it now.
That's lovely to hear. Learning together can be fun for both of you. Next, you could show him how to make a simple chart, so he can see where the money goes each month.
I want to bake a cake for my dad's birthday but we don't have an oven.
You can still bake a cake. Many people use a pressure cooker or a heavy pan on the stove. Have you seen it done before?
No. Is it hard?

It needs some care, but it's doable. People usually put a layer of salt in the cooker, place a stand on it and set the cake tin on top. Remove the gasket and the whistle, then cook on low heat. Ask an adult to help the first time.
How do I know when it's done?
Push a toothpick or knife into the centre. If it comes out clean, the cake is ready. If wet batter sticks to it, cover it again and check after five minutes.
Our society wants to plant trees along the road. I'm on the planning team.
That's a lovely project. Do you know how many trees you're planting?
Around twenty. We're not sure which ones to choose.
Native trees that suit your local climate are usually best, since they grow well and support local birds. A nearby nursery can suggest good ones for your area.
Who will water them?
You could make a simple rota, where each family looks after one or two trees. Give each tree a small name tag. People take more care when a tree feels like "theirs."
Should we involve the children too?
Yes, they usually love it. Let children help plant, paint the tree guards or water the trees in the evening. Watching a tree they planted grow can make them care about it for years.
My grandmother keeps telling the same stories again and again.
That can feel repetitive, but those stories often matter a lot to her. People tend to return to memories that are important to them. Listening patiently can mean a great deal to her.
Is there a way to make it more interesting for me?

You could ask questions she hasn't answered before, like "What did you wear that day?" or "What happened next?" You might hear new details. You could also record her telling them, so the family keeps them for years.
Our school sports day is next week and I signed up for the long jump.
That's exciting! Long jump is all about speed and timing. Have you tried it before?
Only once. I keep stepping over the board.

Measure your run-up. Stand at the board and run away from it at your normal speed, counting your steps. Mark where you are after about twelve steps. Starting from that mark helps you reach the board on the right step.
I'm the shortest player on our basketball team. Can I still be good?
Yes, absolutely. Shorter players are often quicker and better at handling the ball. Many teams rely on them to bring the ball up the court and pass well.
What should I practise most?
Work on dribbling with both hands, quick passes and shooting from outside. Speed and good decisions can matter as much as height. Practising these every day will help you stand out.
I keep starting books and never finishing them. Is that bad?
Not at all. It's fine to stop a book that isn't working for you. Reading should feel worthwhile, not like a chore.
But I don't finish even the ones I like.

Then it might be a time problem, not an interest problem. Try reading at one fixed moment each day, like on the bus or before bed, and keep the book where you can see it. Shorter books can also help you build the habit of finishing.
Grandpa plays chess every evening, and I'd like to learn so I can join him.
What a nice way to spend time with him. Do you know how the pieces move?
Only the pawns and the rook.
Then ask your grandfather to teach you one new piece each day. Play small games with just pawns and that piece. It's easier to remember a move when you use it straight away.
I'm worried I'll lose every game.
You probably will at first, and that's how everyone learns. Ask him to explain his moves after each game. Losing to a good player teaches you a lot.
Can I practise without him?
Yes. You can solve simple chess puzzles from a book or play against a friend. Then show your grandfather what you learned. He will probably enjoy that.
The power went out and our whole street is dark.
Power cuts can be unsettling, especially at night. Do you have a torch or an emergency light?
Just the torch on my phone. The battery is at forty percent.
Then save your phone battery. Use the phone light only when you need it, lower the screen brightness and close apps you aren't using.
We found some candles.
Good. Put them on a plate or in a holder, away from curtains and paper, and never leave them burning in an empty room. Keep them out of reach of small children.
How long do power cuts usually last?
It varies a lot, from minutes to many hours. You could ask a neighbour if they've heard anything, or check for updates from your electricity provider.
Our friend circle has a group chat and I feel ignored there.
That can feel lonely, even with lots of messages flying around. What happens when you post something?
People reply to others but skip my messages.
Group chats move fast, and messages get lost easily, so it may not be personal. Still, it hurts. Do you feel included when you meet them in person?
Yes, in person it's fine.
That's a good sign. It may just be how the chat works, not how they feel about you. You could spend less energy on the group chat and more on meeting or messaging friends one to one.
Any ideas for using up leftover rice? We always cook too much.
Leftover rice is very useful. Lemon rice, curd rice and fried rice are all quick ways to use it. Which flavours do you like?
Fried rice sounds good. We have some vegetables.
Chop the vegetables small. Heat a little oil, fry some garlic and onion, add the vegetables, then the cold rice. Season with salt and pepper or a little soy sauce, and stir until everything is hot.
Why cold rice? Can't I use fresh?
Cold rice works better because it's drier, so the grains stay separate instead of turning mushy. Fresh rice is softer and tends to clump.
How long can I keep cooked rice?
Keep it covered in the fridge and use it within a day. Cool it quickly after cooking rather than leaving it out for hours.
Should I get one goldfish or two?
Goldfish are social and often do better with company, so two is usually better than one. But they grow bigger than people expect and make a lot of mess, so they need a large tank with a filter.
I only have a small bowl.

A small bowl isn't a good home for goldfish. The water gets dirty fast and there's little space to swim. It's kinder to save up for a proper tank first, or ask at a fish shop which small fish suit a small tank.
I'm teaching myself the ukulele from online videos.
The ukulele is a great choice for teaching yourself. It's small and has only four strings. How far have you got?
I know three chords: C, A minor and F.
That's a strong start. Those three chords appear in lots of simple songs. Practise switching between them slowly until the changes feel smooth.
Switching is the hard part. My fingers are slow.
That's normal. Try switching between just two chords for one minute, counting how many clean changes you make. Do it every day and you'll see the number go up.
When should I learn the next chord?
Once you can switch between your three chords without stopping, add G. With C, A minor, F and G, you can play a huge number of songs.
That's motivating!
It should be. Pick one easy song with those chords as your goal for the month. Playing a real song keeps practice fun.
